question: X, Y and Z invested a sum in the ratio of 58 : 72 : 20, respectively. If they earned a total profit of ₹3,750 at the end of the year, what is the difference between the shares of Y and Z?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio = 58 : 72 : 20

Total profit units = 58 + 72 + 20 = 150 units

Difference in profit units of Y and Z = 72 − 20 = 52 units

Required difference = (52 / 150) × 3750

Required difference = 52 × 25 = ₹1300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment ratio of X, Y and Z = 58 : 72 : 20

Total profit earned = ₹3750

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio (when the time period is constant for all partners)

 
• 
 
 
 X
 58x
 
 
 Y
 72x
 
 
 Z
 20x
 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 

 
 Diff = 52x
 
 Total Profit = 150x = ₹3750

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the profit shares of X, Y and Z be 58x, 72x, and 20x respectively.

⇒ Total profit = 58x + 72x + 20x = 150x

⇒ 150x = 3750

⇒ x = 3750 ÷ 150 = 25

⇒ Profit share of Y = 72x = 72 × 25 = ₹1800

⇒ Profit share of Z = 20x = 20 × 25 = ₹500

⇒ Difference between shares of Y and Z = 1800 − 500 = 1300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When investments are made for the exact same time period by all partners, the profit is distributed directly in the ratio of their invested capitals.

Compound Partnership

When investments are made for different time periods, the profit sharing ratio is equivalent to the product of their capital and time period (Profit Ratio = C₁×T₁ : C₂×T₂).

Working Partner vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner receives a fixed percentage of the profit or a regular salary for managing the business. The remaining profit is then distributed among all the partners strictly in the ratio of their effective capital.
